blocks.text: Service Line Assessment: Johnson, Cross and Gibbs

items: Prepared for Angela Mahoney, General Manager
A review of which service lines earn their keep, and which are carried by the rest
Commenced {{fact:f:E-2020-001.start}}; roughly seven months end to end
You asked a plain question: which of your service lines earn their keep once their true costs are counted, and which are carried by the rest.
We answer it from your own cost accounting and actual volumes, set against net revenue rather than charges, not from national benchmarks alone.
Where a line's economics turn on how physicians are paid, or on revenue the line has earned and then lost in billing, we follow the question there rather than stop at the ledger.
Daniel Alvarado leads the service-line economics and is your day-to-day contact.
Susan Clark takes any question that touches physician compensation and fair-market-value review.
Patricia Moore traces revenue-cycle leakage, claim by claim, through every handoff.
We have agreed the service-line definitions with you, so both sides are measuring the same thing before any number is compared.
Data is in hand for the largest lines, and the smaller ones are still being pulled together with your team, some of it from paperwork that reaches us as scans.
The cost reconstruction is under way. We are not yet ready to name winners and losers, and we will not name them until the numbers are firm.
A line can look unprofitable on paper when the real problem is revenue it earned and then lost in billing. We are careful to tell those two apart.
Some contracting paperwork reaches us as scans rather than files, which slows the pull; your team has been helpful in filling the gaps.
We will keep fair-market-value language for the compensation questions that actually warrant it, and nowhere else.
Finish the cost reconstruction across every line, large and small.
Reconcile the revenue-cycle picture against the service-line results, so a leaking line is not mistaken for an unprofitable one.
Bring you a first read of the findings for {{fact:f:E-2020-001.client}} at the midpoint review, with recommendations kept separate from findings.
